title: Carbon monoxide
tldr: If a CO alarm sounds or carbon monoxide exposure is suspected, get everyone into fresh air immediately and call emergency services. Do not stay inside to find the source. Headache, dizziness, nausea or confusion can be warning signs.
steps: Move people and pets into fresh air, without delaying to ventilate or troubleshoot.
Report the alarm, symptoms and possible fuel-burning source to emergency services.
Tell responders about suspected exposure even if symptoms improve outdoors.
Do not reenter until responders say it is safe.
next: Install CO alarms and service heating equipment. Keep generators and grills outdoors, far from openings.
watch: CO is invisible and odorless. A silent smoke alarm is not proof that air is safe.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
without_help: Leave the building even if responders cannot be reached. Gather outside away from exhaust, keep everyone out and seek reachable medical care for symptoms. Do not send someone back inside to ventilate or switch equipment off.
household: Choose an outside meeting place and check that every person can use the escape route. Keep keys, mobility aids and shoes accessible. Tell neighbours about a hazard from a safe location; do not organise an untrained entry or rescue.
pack_now: Keep essential medicines, drinking water, a battery light, shoes, phone power and a written contact card within reach. Adapt the load to the hazard and the people with you; do not delay escape to collect equipment.
